resolutions.researcher_notes: Both brief-current URLs (attaqa.net, kingabdullah.jo) now actually resolve 200 OK (re-checked with url_verifier), contra the brief's DEAD_LINK flag, but neither confirms current ('operating') status: kingabdullah.jo is the 2003 inauguration announcement (historical only, contains 'طابا'/Taba); attaqa.net (Nov 2024) discusses possible future re-routing, not current flow, and does not mention Taba specifically. Replaced with two independent 2024-2025 trade-press sources describing the Taba-Aqaba (Egypt-Jordan) link as an active, in-use physical connection: World Pipelines (Dec 2024) reports Jordan-Egypt LNG/FSRU deal moving 'gas supplies...through the existing pipeline network linking the two countries'; Egypt Oil & Gas (2025, Energos Force FSRU arrival) reports the FSRU's 'connection to the Arab Gas Pipeline will enable Egypt to tap into LNG supplies' at Aqaba. Neither is a bare 'currently flowing today' snapshot, so tier=medium rather than high. IMPORTANT CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Enab Baladi (Jan 2026, English) reports Jordan's Ministry of Energy explicitly denying that gas newly reaching Syria via Aqaba is Egyptian -- it is regasified LNG, not gas pumped through the Egypt-Taba-Aqaba subsea pipe. So the Taba-Aqaba segment's *direct* Egypt-to-Jordan gas flow appears intermittent/underutilized in 2025-2026 even though the physical link remains in commercial use (LNG-swap arrangement) -- worth a human check if GEM wants finer status granularity than 'operating' vs 'idle'. Searched: Arabic (attaqa.net, kingabdullah.jo) + English trade press (World Pipelines, Egypt Oil & Gas, OGJ, S&P Global, Enab Baladi) via WebSearch/WebFetch; no fabricated URLs; gem.wiki/GEM used only as a lead, not cited.

Oil & Gas Journal states directly: 'Under an agreement with East Gas Co., Gasco undertook the operation and maintenance of the Arab gas pipeline extending from Arish to Aqaba' -- explicit, on-point support for Operator = Egyptian Natural Gas Co (GASCO) covering the Taba-Aqaba subsea segment (Taba sits between Arish and Aqaba on this same stretch). Wikipedia's Arab Gas Pipeline article corroborates GASCO as part of the Egyptian consortium (with EGAS, ENPPI, Petrojet) that developed/runs this section, though it does not isolate a single 'operator' as crisply as OGJ. EGAS's own site (egas.com.eg/history-natural-gas-industry, already in seed_citations) independently confirms GASCO's general role as Egypt's gas Transmission System Operator (TSO) since 1997 and that AGP started operations in 2003, but does not name GASCO specifically for this segment, so it was left out as a third ref to avoid diluting precision. offshore-technology.com / hydrocarbons-technology.com (seed citation) were checked too but only list GASCO as one of four consortium builders without naming an operator, and offshore-technology.com is the same publisher family as hydrocarbons-technology.com (not fully independent), so not used. No contradicting Operator claim found in any source (no rival operator named for this segment).
